name: Looper
notes: Upstream's released library, dropped in **unmodified** (sha256 97f2aa03e5f581398690bc66f856bd408d23490e9dc08e20bb7075a2d07f97e5, 198 532 bytes): appending and copying materials is all this add-on does with it. Measured with shader_manifest_names.py: the collection, the two objects in it, the three material names, the image node names inside both shader materials and the outline group's socket names and identifiers are the same as 0.2.4's, which is why every section but `blend`, the id/name and `settings` is copied from that manifest unchanged. Its `Uma Shader` group has two sockets ours does not: `Toggle World Light Influence` (float, min 0, max 1, default 0.0, after `Toggle If Face`) and `Global Color` (colour, white, after `Light Threshold`) - both rows are in `settings` below, in the interface's own order, so a chooser that reads this manifest draws 20 rows instead of 18. Note that its file carries no actions (ours carries the ear/tail library) and no `Uma Sun` override of ours: nothing but the shading is expected from it. Its outline group is 64 nodes against our 71 and lacks our `Only Depth Offset` and `Value` sockets, so `outline.blend` above names `Umashaders.blend` and the shell comes out of *that* file instead: our outline, upstream's shading. Before 2.24.0 this manifest left the outline to 0.2.6's own file, which silently gave upstream's shell while our code wrote at socket names that were not there - it reports rather than raising, so nothing looked broken.

settings.description: Off: the shader's own light direction (the sun empty) decides which side is lit. On: the scene's real lighting does, sampled through a Diffuse BSDF and Shader to RGB - the release note's option for the shader to react to world lighting. 0 is off, 1 is on
How dark a shaded area has to be before it counts as shadow. Lower catches more of the model; higher keeps more of the flat colour
Tint multiplied over the whole character, over both the lit and the shaded side - the release note's global colour tint
Strength of the lit (diffuse) side of the character
Colour saturation of the lit side. 0 is greyscale, 1 is the texture's own colours
Tint of the lit side, multiplied over the texture
Strength of the shadowed side
Colour saturation of the shadowed side
Tint of the shadowed side, multiplied over the texture
Strength of the metallic response
Tint of the metallic response
Strength of the specular highlight
Tint of the specular highlight
Width of the ambient rim, the light that wraps the whole silhouette
Strength of the ambient rim
Tint of the ambient rim
Width of the directional rim, the edge light on the lit side
Strength of the directional rim
Tint of the directional rim
Strength of the glow on the parts that have an emission texture (the eyes, mostly)
